name: COMO Cocoa Island, The Maldives
positioning: Overwater villa resort on Makunufushi in South Malé Atoll, with villas shaped like traditional dhoni boats and a COMO Shambhala wellness centre
best_for: Snorkellers and divers who want reef access straight from the villa
Wellness-focused stays built around COMO Shambhala
Families or groups wanting multi-bedroom villas with private pools

facts.text: COMO Cocoa Island, known locally as Makunufushi, is located among South Malé's coral atolls.
The island is a 40-minute speedboat transfer from Malé International Airport; guests do not need a seaplane to reach it.
Each villa sits above the lagoon, connected by planked walkways.
The villas are built with high rafters, glossy teak floors, New Zealand pine and Kajan-thatched roofs.
The two-bedroom COMO Sunrise Villa has separate wings and a private pool directly above the ocean.
The COMO Sunset Villa is two standalone villas connected by a wooden walkway, named for its sunset views.
COMO Shambhala treatment rooms overlook the lagoon and greenery.
A two-storey wellness building has a yoga pavilion on the top floor and a gym on the lower floor.
A complimentary guided house reef snorkel can turn up Kashmir snapper, oriental sweetlips, needlefish and the occasional harmless reef shark.
Dive sites in the atoll include the Kandooma Caves and the shark cleaning station at Cocoa Thila.
Ufaa is an inside-outside, pool- and beach-side restaurant serving modern interpretations of Indian and Mediterranean cuisine.
The watersports centre offers complimentary use of non-motorised equipment.

highlights.text: The overwater villas are shaped like the curving wooden forms of the local dhoni fishing boats.
From the private terrace of each villa, guests can step off and swim in the sea.
The COMO Shambhala hydrotherapy pool is one of the few in the Maldives.
On the UV night snorkel, special UV torches and mask lenses reveal the fluorescent colours of corals on the house reef.
Guests can sponsor a coral propagating frame and help the resident marine biologist plant it in the resort's coral garden.

considerations.text: Not all villas have private pools.
